goal: Find a path to 10x or greater speedup of simulate!() while preserving mathematical correctness, physical fidelity, and API flexibility. No cheating — no skipping energy bins, no reducing physics effects, no lowering precision below what's physically meaningful. All GPU code MUST use AcceleratedKernels.jl.

context.scope: simulate!() ONLY — forward projection + detector physics pipeline. Reconstruction (reconstruct!) is a SEPARATE function and is OUT OF SCOPE.
context.architecture: AcceleratedKernels.jl (AK.jl) for GPU-agnostic execution (Metal/CUDA/ROCm/CPU). Zero-allocation workspace pattern. Polychromatic via sequential energy bin loop.
context.hard_constraint: AcceleratedKernels.jl is NON-NEGOTIABLE. All GPU compute must go through AK.jl. No backend-specific kernels.
context.math_constraint: Same mathematical results (within floating-point tolerance). Same API. Same physics fidelity. The improvement must come from BETTER algorithms or BETTER parallelism, not from doing LESS physics.

topics.title: Profile simulate!() — Where Does the Time Actually Go?
topics.description: FIRST TOPIC. Before optimizing anything, MEASURE. Profile simulate!() end-to-end on a realistic phantom. Break down time by: (1) forward projection total, (2) within projection: μ-volume creation vs ray tracing vs accumulation, (3) each of the 16 detector physics effects individually. Produce a time breakdown showing exactly where the seconds go. The 10x target needs a baseline. DO NOT include reconstruction — it's a separate function.

topics.title: Fuse the Sequential Energy Loop — One Ray Trace, All Energies
topics.description: ONLY pursue this topic AFTER SPEED-000 profiling shows the energy loop is a significant bottleneck. The current polychromatic projection loops over energy bins sequentially, each doing a full ray trace. Research: Can this be fused into one trace per ray that accumulates across all energies via material-to-μ lookup? What are the memory vs compute tradeoffs? How do CatSim, TIGRE, and MC simulators handle polychromatic projection? All proposed kernels must use AK.jl primitives.
sources: De Man et al. 2001 (ray-driven CT projection)

topics.title: Siddon vs Distance-Driven vs Separable Footprint — Algorithm-Level Speedup
topics.description: ONLY pursue AFTER SPEED-000 shows ray tracing is significant. Research alternatives to Siddon: (A) Distance-driven (De Man & Basu 2002). (B) Separable footprint (Long et al. 2010). (C) Joseph's method. (D) Branchless DDA. For each: speedup vs Siddon? Mathematical equivalence? GPU-friendliness via AK.jl (divergence-free)? What do clinical simulators use?

topics.title: GPU Kernel Optimization via AK.jl — Occupancy, Memory, Divergence
topics.description: Even with the same algorithm, GPU kernel optimization can yield 2-5x. ALL through AK.jl. Research: (A) Current AK.jl kernel launch patterns — are we maximizing occupancy? (B) Memory access patterns — coalesced or scattered? (C) Can AK.jl's foreachindex handle our workload shape efficiently? (D) Warp/SIMD divergence in Siddon — do rays in the same workgroup follow different paths? (E) What AK.jl primitives are we NOT using that could help? (F) Is there overhead in the AK.jl abstraction layer itself?

topics.title: Physics Pipeline — Batch Effects, Fuse Kernels, Reduce Launches
topics.description: The 16-step physics pipeline applies effects sequentially via AK.jl. Each step may be a separate kernel launch with synchronization. Research: (A) Can adjacent effects be fused into fewer AK.jl kernels? (B) Is kernel launch overhead significant? (C) Can the pipeline be a single fused kernel? (D) Are any effects mathematically combinable (e.g., flat_filter × bowtie_filter in one pass)? (E) Memory bandwidth cost of reading/writing the sinogram 16 times?

topics.title: What Do Fast CT Simulators Do? — CatSim, TIGRE, gVXR
topics.description: Survey performance-oriented CT simulators for their forward projection + detector physics speed. For each: (A) CatSim/XCIST — our parity target. (B) TIGRE — CUDA-optimized projection. (C) gVXR — GPU ray tracing for X-ray. (D) MCX/MCgpu — Monte Carlo GPU tricks. Collect concrete timing numbers for comparable phantom sizes and detector configurations. Focus on forward projection and detector physics only — NOT reconstruction.

topics.title: Float32 vs Float64 — Where Can We Use Lower Precision Without Losing Physics?
topics.description: NOT cheating — this is about using the RIGHT precision for each stage of simulate!(). Research: (A) What precision does Siddon traversal need? (B) What precision do detector physics effects need? (noise is stochastic — Float32 may suffice). (C) What precision do clinical scanners actually use? (12-16 bit ADC). (D) Can we use mixed precision — Float64 for ray geometry, Float32 for physics? All through AK.jl.

topics.title: SYNTHESIS: 10x Speedup Roadmap for simulate!()
topics.description: After profiling and top bottleneck topics complete: synthesize into a concrete optimization plan for simulate!() only. For each optimization: estimated speedup factor, implementation complexity, correctness proof, AK.jl compatibility. Stack multiplicatively. Produce a prioritized implementation order with test gates. All implementations must use AK.jl.
